requestedActions.title: Read titles and content of pages customers explicitly share with the app

guide.summary: Customers authorize the app with OAuth 2.0 and each user's token is tied to that user. The requested read-content capability is the least-privilege documented grant, and access is limited to pages each customer selects in the page picker.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read titles and content of pages customers explicitly share with the app. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Use OAuth 2.0 user authorization for customers in other workspaces
findings.detail: OAuth integrations are documented for acting on behalf of each user, and the token is tied to that user. Scoped integrations can only be installed in selected workspaces, so other customer workspaces require a public integration.

evidence.quote: Use an OAuth integration when your internal tool needs to act on behalf of each person who uses it. Each user authorizes the app separately and grants it access to
your app available to any workspace, create a public integration .
An OAuth integration can be installed in any Notion workspace within its installation scope — a specific set chosen at creation time for scoped integrations, or any workspace for public

findings.title: Each customer must complete the authorization flow individually
findings.detail: After a user authorizes the OAuth integration, only that user can interact with the connection in their workspace. Each member of a workspace must complete the flow separately.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers in multiple workspaces or members use the app.

evidence.quote: After a user authorizes a OAuth integration, only that user can interact with the connection in their workspace. If multiple members in a workspace want to use the same OAuth
workspace want to use an OAuth integration, each prospective user needs to individually follow the auth flow for the connection.

findings.title: Read content capability for reading shared page content
findings.detail: Reading page content through the API requires the connection to have read content capabilities. Without this capability, the call returns 403. The grant covers the endpoints for reading page content in this request.
findings.appliesWhen: The app reads page titles and content and does not create or modify pages.

evidence.quote: Requirements Your connection must have read content capabilities on the target page in order to call this endpoint. To update your connection’s capabilities, navigate to the Developer portal , select
​ Errors The connection needs read content capabilities . Missing capabilities return 403 . A missing page or missing access returns 404 .

findings.title: Customers choose which pages to share during authorization
findings.detail: The page picker lets each user select pages and databases to share with the connection. The connection only has access to pages the customer selected, and the user must have full access to share them.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers choose which pages to share.

evidence.quote: If the user opts to Select pages , then a page picker interface opens. A user can search for and select pages and databases to share with the connection from
The page picker only displays pages or databases to which a user has full access , because a user needs full access to a resource in order to be able
3 The user selects which pages to grant the connection access to using the page picker.

steps.title: Create a public OAuth integration for customers in other workspaces
steps.detail: In the Developer portal Build > Connections, create a new connection with the Any workspace installation scope (public integration), so customers in other workspaces can install it. Scoped integrations cannot be installed outside selected workspaces and installation scope cannot be changed later. Enter the redirect URI(s) and select only the read content capability.
steps.doneWhen: A public OAuth connection exists with a redirect URI configured and read content capability enabled, with no write or user administration capabilities selected.

steps.title: Store OAuth client credentials server-side
steps.detail: Open the Configuration tab of the connection to find the OAuth client ID, client secret and authorization URL. Store them as server-side environment variables; never put them in source code, browser bundles or version control.
steps.doneWhen: OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, NOTION_AUTH_URL and the redirect URI are set in the server environment only.

evidence.quote: Open the Configuration tab to find your OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret . Use them to implement the OAuth authorization flow .

After creating an OAuth integration in the Developer portal , access the connection’s secrets in the Configuration tab. Similarly to the internal connections, these values should be protected and should
never be included in source code or version control.

fields: OAUTH_CLIENT_ID from Configuration tab
OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET from Configuration tab
NOTION_AUTH_URL from Configuration tab

steps.title: Send a test user through the consent flow and check the callback
steps.detail: Direct a test customer to the authorization URL from the Configuration tab. The user chooses Select pages in the page picker and selects a test page they own, then clicks Allow access. Notion redirects to the redirect URI with a code query parameter. Confirm the callback contains code and the state value you sent, or an error parameter if the user cancelled.
steps.doneWhen: The callback URL contains a code query parameter and the matching state value, and only the test page the user selected is accessible to the app.

evidence.quote: Parameter Description Required client_id An identifier for your connection, found in the connection settings. ✅
If the user opts to Select pages , then a page picker interface opens. A user can search for and select pages and databases to share with the connection from
Parameter Description Required code A temporary authorization code. ✅

fields: client_id from Configuration tab
redirect_uri: your registered callback URL
state: a random value you generate and verify
owner=user and response_type=code are fixed

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Send a POST to the token endpoint with HTTP Basic authentication using CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET. The JSON body must include grant_type set to authorization_code, the code from the callback, and redirect_uri matching the registered value. Store the returned access_token, refresh_token and bot_id; the token is not executed against any resource yet.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains access_token, refresh_token, bot_id, owner and workspace_id, and these are stored server-side tied to the test user.

evidence.quote: The request is authorized using HTTP Basic Authentication. The credential is a colon-delimited combination of the connection’s CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET , like so:
The body of the request contains the following JSON-encoded fields:
Content-Type : application/json { "grant_type" : "authorization_code" , "code" : "e202e8c9-0990-40af-855f-ff8f872b1ec6" , "redirect_uri" : "https://example.com/auth/notion/callback" }

fields: code: from the callback query string of the consent step
redirect_uri: must match the registered redirect URI
Basic auth uses client_id and client_secret from Configuration

steps.title: Read shared test page as markdown
steps.detail: Use TEST_PAGE_ID and ACCESS_TOKEN to GET the markdown endpoint with markdown_version=v2. Read the top-level $.markdown string, $.id, $.object (expected page), $.truncated and $.unknown_block_ids. If truncated is true or unknown_block_ids is non-empty, run the continuation step for each unknown block ID and append each returned markdown string in order. Ignore $.warnings for content.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 with object page and a markdown string; truncated is false, or every unknown_block_ids entry was fetched by the continuation step with 404 results recorded as not readable. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented read content capability; confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to the markdown endpoint and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: When truncation or permissions cause unknown blocks, the truncated field is set to true and the unknown_block_ids array contains the affected block IDs.
You can attempt to fetch unloaded blocks by passing their IDs back to this same endpoint as the page_id path parameter. Blocks that are unknown due to permissions will return
string required The ID of the page (or block) to retrieve as markdown. Non-navigable block IDs from truncated responses can be passed here to fetch their subtrees.

fields: TEST_PAGE_ID: a page the test user selected in the picker
ACCESS_TOKEN: from the token exchange response, same token for continuation requests
markdown_version=v2 is recommended

steps.title: Read title of the shared page from its properties
steps.detail: GET the page object for TEST_PAGE_ID. Do not assume the property name is title. Find the entry in the properties object whose type is title, then join the plain_text value of every element of that entry's title array in order. A page outside a data source returns only the title property. Read the page title only; do not request content from other endpoints.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 with object page, and the title text is produced by joining plain_text across all elements of the title-type property array. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented read content capability; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested GET page request and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: For a page in a data source, the property values follow that data source’s schema . For a page whose parent is another page, the only property is title .
Pages that aren't in a data source always return only title .
string required The ID of the page to retrieve.

fields: TEST_PAGE_ID: the same shared test page
ACCESS_TOKEN: from the token exchange response for the test account

steps.title: Confirm an unshared page is not readable
steps.detail: Using the same access token, request a page the test user did not select in the page picker, such as a private page they own that was not shared. Expected output is HTTP 404, showing the token cannot read pages outside the customer's selection. Do not use a nonexistent ID as the test.
steps.doneWhen: The request for the unshared page returns HTTP 404 and the response does not contain its content.

steps.title: Fetch unloaded markdown blocks recursively
steps.detail: For each ID in unknown_block_ids from a markdown response, GET the markdown endpoint with that ID as page_id, markdown_version=v2, and the same ACCESS_TOKEN. Append each returned markdown string. If a returned body has truncated true or non-empty unknown_block_ids, repeat for those IDs until every response has truncated false and an empty unknown_block_ids array. A 404 for a permission-limited unknown block means it is not readable with this connection; record it and do not retry it.
steps.doneWhen: Every unknown block ID is either fetched with HTTP 200 and its markdown appended, or recorded as not readable after a 404. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to the markdown endpoint with block IDs from unknown_block_ids and no prohibited actions.
